I’ve been coming here for a while, but I’m officially tired of the nonsense.

For what has to be around the 10th time, the manager hits me with the famous: “Card machine isn’t working. CASH ONLY.”

My man… at this point, just put a permanent CASH ONLY sign on the door and stop insulting my intelligence. 😂 That card machine has apparently called out sick more times than an NYC employee with unlimited PTO.

Then there was the turtle incident.

Last year, I bought a turtle that I personally saw alive and moving around in the store. I get home, open everything up, and somehow my turtle is dead as a doorknob.

I bring it right back, and instead of “Wow, sorry about that,” this man has the AUDACITY to accuse ME of switching the turtle!

Sir… WHAT?! 😂

Here’s the part I still can’t understand: he exchanged it anyway. So you genuinely believed I pulled off some elaborate turtle-switching conspiracy, brought you a completely different dead turtle, and your response was… “Okay, here’s another one”?

Come on, man.

Between the mysteriously terminally ill credit-card machine and getting accused of running a black-market turtle exchange operation, I’ve had enough questionable experiences here to finally write this review.

And the crazy part is, I met the actual owner when I first started shopping here and thought he was SUPER cool. Completely different experience. I genuinely wish I could speak to him directly because I’d love for him to know what customers are dealing with when he isn’t around.

I actually liked this store, which is why I kept coming back. But there’s only so many times somebody can tell me the card machine is “broken” before I start wondering whether the machine needs a technician, a priest, or a proper burial next to my first turtle.

We bought a bearded dragon, and the seller seemed very pushy about us taking this particular one. After bringing her home, we discovered she had been bullied by larger bearded dragons in her enclosure. They had bitten off part of her tail, and her back legs don’t work properly due to MBD (Metabolic Bone Disease).

Please do not get a pet from here. The animals appear to be kept in poor conditions, and it’s heartbreaking to see. They deserve much better care.

​I am deeply disappointed by my recent visit to this store. While the exterior looks decent, the conditions inside are deeply concerning and unethical. On an 83° day, the store had no proper climate control, and the indoor temperature felt well over 80°. The birds were displayed in the front window in direct sunlight, clearly in distress and huddling together at the bottom of their enclosure just to find shade. Several fish in the aquatic section were also floating dead. Beyond the terrible animal care, the customer service was appalling. After a staff member agreed to help us purchase a bird, the owner approached my partner and me. When we explained we already had the necessary supplies at home, he aggressively badgered us, insisting we could only buy his specific seeds and could not provide a special diet. The situation grew worse when the owner asked where we live. When I gave a general area, he looked at us two young Black adults and said, "Oh, that's a neighborhood you sell weed in, not open a pet store." Not only do we not smoke, but this blatant profiling and microaggression was entirely uncalled for. It is incredibly ironic for him to lecture us on pet care when his own store is actively violating basic animal welfare standards. We immediately walked out. Save your time and money, and support stores that treat both animals and customers with respect.
